html:
A Chinese revolutionary, feminist and poet, executed by the Qing dynasty in 1907. She is honoured in China as a national heroine.

Born to a well off family and given an unusual education, she was married off young. In 1904 she left her husband and children, sold her jewellery and went to study in Japan. In Tokyo she joined the revolutionary circles around Sun Yat-sen, wore men's clothing, practised with swords and spoke against foot binding and for women's education.

Back in China she founded a women's newspaper in Shanghai and ran a school in Shaoxing that trained revolutionaries in secret. In 1907 she and her cousin Xu Xilin planned uprisings. Xu's failed, he was killed, and Qiu was arrested days later. She refused to confess and was beheaded in Shaoxing at the age of 31. Her death shocked many and helped turn opinion against the dynasty, which fell in the Xinhai Revolution four years later.
